source_signal_audit.OnPlayerGetDamage: Incomplete and not uniformly resolved: it is pre-cancellation for WEAPONHIT, absent from zombie, sleep, and direct body-part producers, and some vehicle/general-health values are requested inputs rather than verified aggregate loss.
source_signal_audit.OnWeaponHitCharacter: Pre-resolution and pre-cancellation; cannot represent resolved loss.
source_signal_audit.body_part_calls: AddDamage, ReduceHealth, DamageFromWeapon, zombie damage, vehicle damage, and direct SetHealth paths have no single complete post-resolution Lua producer.
source_signal_audit.aggregate_health: Post-resolution net state is available, but same-update healing can cancel or hide incoming loss.
source_signal_audit.conclusion: No complete non-double-counting source-faithful signal was found. GB-R3 remains requires-user-decision; no approximation or intent narrowing was implemented.

registration_invariant.success_state: exactly one canonical keyed row with the stable dispatcher
registration_invariant.failure_state: zero rows matching the handler id or dispatcher function
registration_invariant.rollback_surface: exact bounded pairs snapshot of UTCore._coreHandlers plus _coreHandlerCount and _coreHandlersDirty
registration_invariant.unrelated_state: preserve every unrelated numeric, sparse, high-hole, and nonnumeric key/value identity

performance_model: No new handler is added. The existing central dispatch performs one marker lookup for inactive players, one aggregate-health getter per active Glass Body update, and a bounded body-part distribution only after resolved loss.
runtime_proof: Blocked for the all-incoming-loss claim: current Build 42 has no complete non-double-counting post-resolution damage signal, and aggregate same-update healing can hide damage. Full Exit to Desktop, current-version save/load, rendered English, and profiler capture also remain unobserved.

open_policy_question.question: How should Glass Body preserve all resolved incoming body-health loss when Build 42 exposes no complete source-faithful resolved-damage signal?
